First, note that the range of $\theta =\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x$ is given by

$$
-{90}^{∘}\le \theta \le {90}^{∘}.
$$

Now, let's take a look at the unit circle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14035417/assets/ca39c4cde40b99fd40a11746a31398d82814268b2df706e3101ee88648c9e2d4.png)

From the values on the unit circle, we see that

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡({300}^{∘})=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

However, ${300}^{∘}$ does not lie within the range of $\theta .$ To get an angle that's coterminal with ${300}^{∘}$ that lies within the range of $\theta ,$ we subtract ${360}^{∘}.$

$$
{300}^{∘}-{360}^{∘}=-{60}^{∘}.
$$

Hence,

$$
\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})=-{60}^{∘}.
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) & =4\cdot (-{60}^{∘}) \\  & ={-240}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
